name: Galveston Island Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-undisputed
events.note: The belt the fed's cards called the Galveston Island Championship became the GIW Undisputed Championship when it was unified with the Deep South title in the Eric Sparrow and Chris Jericho match of the card of Revolt, 17 February 2011; the fed's own Undisputed history carries the one run of reigns under both names.

epitaph: GIW's Galveston Island Championship: 5 reigns are served here, across 4 different champions, the first beginning on 3 June 2010 with Aspen Chaud and the last on 13 February 2011 with Chris Jericho. The longest of those is Wake Walker's, 98 days from 22 August 2010. Of these, 2 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). The fed's own Undisputed history carries it as the first seven lines of one belt; on 17 February 2011 it became the GIW Undisputed Championship.

name: GIW Undisputed Championship
epitaph: GIW's Undisputed Championship: 18 reigns are served here, across 14 different champions, the first beginning on 17 February 2011 with Eric Sparrow and the last on 18 August 2019 with Bronx Valescence. By the dates served here the longest is Alexis Terry's, 257 days from 23 June 2013, which the fed's own history counts as 54 days; of the reigns whose dates fit the history's own lengths, the longest is Alioth Starre's, 155 days from 29 May 2011. Of these, 4 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It is the Galveston Island Championship under the name it took on 17 February 2011; it took in the Deep South belt on that date and again on 29 October 2014, and the North Beach belt on 7 March 2014.

name: GIW North Beach Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-epw-evolve
events.note: The 2010 North Beach belt was renamed the EPW Evolve Championship; the fed's own Deep South history records "Title Changed from GIW North Beach to EPW Evolve", and the card of Tuesday Night Evolve, 31 August 2010 has the champion called the Evolve champion rather than the North Beach champion. The fed's own history places the note before Chris Armstrong's win of 22 August 2010; the cards place the change of name after it.

epitaph: GIW's North Beach Championship: 3 reigns are served here, across 3 different champions, the first beginning on 17 June 2010 with Apollo Calix and the last on 22 August 2010 with Chris Armstrong. The longest of those is Chris Armstrong's, 44 days from 22 August 2010. This is the 2010 belt, not the North Beach Championship of 2011 to 2019 (a separate belt that shares the name); it became the EPW Evolve Championship on 31 August 2010.

name: EPW Evolve Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-evolve
events.note: Renamed the GIW Evolve Championship: the fed's own Deep South history reads "Title Vacated Due to Injury, Renamed 'GIW Evolve'"; the card of Revolt, 11 November 2010 has the champion not showing up and qualifiers for the GIW Evolve title following. History and card give different reasons for the vacancy; both stand.

epitaph: GIW's EPW Evolve Championship: 2 reigns are served here, across 2 different champions, the first beginning on 5 October 2010 with Christopher Darren Erns and the last on 19 October 2010 with Chris Armstrong. The longest is Chris Armstrong's, from 19 October 2010 to about 11 November 2010 (24 days in the fed's own history); of the reigns with both dates exact, the longest is Christopher Darren Erns's, 14 days from 5 October 2010. Of these, 1 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It took this name on 31 August 2010 and became the GIW Evolve Championship on 11 November 2010.

name: GIW Evolve Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-deep-south
events.note: Renamed the Deep South Championship: the fed's own Deep South history reads "Title Changed To 'Deep South Championship'", on the card of Monday Night Affliction, 24 January 2011.

epitaph: GIW's Evolve Championship: 2 reigns are served here, across 2 different champions, the first beginning on 28 November 2010 with Eric Sparrow and the last on 9 January 2011 with Christopher Darren Erns. The longest of those is Eric Sparrow's, 42 days from 28 November 2010. Of these, 1 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It became the Deep South Championship on 24 January 2011.

name: GIW Deep South Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-undisputed
events.note: Unified with the Galveston Island Championship to become the GIW Undisputed Championship (the fed's own history: "Unified with 'Galveston Island Championship' to become 'GIW Undisputed Championship'"; the card of Revolt, 17 February 2011).

Retired when the fed closed in August 2013 and brought back when it returned (the fed's own history: "Belt Retired when Company momentarily closes, brought back when company returns"). The date is that of the last card before the closure, 4 August 2013; no card names the retirement itself.

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-undisputed
events.note: Unified with the Undisputed Championship on the card of 29 October 2014 (the fed's own history places it at On Hallowed Ground IV, its Undisputed history at On Hallowed Ground III; the card is headed On Hallowed Ground). The belt was brought back by Aspen Chaud on 15 March 2015.

epitaph: GIW's Deep South Championship: 16 reigns are served here, across 15 different champions, the first beginning on 24 January 2011 with Madison Seton and the last on 30 August 2015 with Geneva Lost. The longest of those is Christopher Darren Erns's, 99 days from 22 July 2014. Of these, 5 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It was unified into the Undisputed Championship on 17 February 2011, retired at the 2013 closure, brought back in 2014, unified again on 29 October 2014 and brought back once more on 15 March 2015.

name: Affliction Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-legacy
events.note: Unified with the Hardcore Championship in a match on the card of Blackout, 22 August 2010, which made the GIW Legacy Championship (the fed's own Hardcore history: "Unified with Affliction Championship Becomes GIW Legacy Championship"). The fed's own North Beach table carries this belt's one reign as its first line and then "VACATED".

epitaph: GIW's Affliction Championship: 1 reign is served here, across 1 different champion, the first beginning on 18 July 2010 with Damon Synn. Of these, 1 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). The fed's own North Beach table opens with this belt; it was unified into the Legacy Championship on 22 August 2010.

name: GIW NOX Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-north-beach
events.note: Became the GIW North Beach Championship at the unification bout of 17 February 2011 (the fed's own Television history: "Unified with 'GIW NOX Championship' to become 'GIW North Beach Championship'"); the unification bout ended in a double count-out and no champion was named that night.

epitaph: GIW's NOX Championship: 3 reigns are served here, across 3 different champions, the first beginning on 17 January 2011 with Mike Bryant and the last on 13 February 2011 with Madison Seton. The longest of those is Mike Bryant's, 14 days from 17 January 2011. Of these, 1 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It became the GIW North Beach Championship on 17 February 2011.

name: GIW North Beach Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-undisputed
events.note: Unified with the Undisputed Championship on the card of Revolt, 7 March 2014, when Michael Lynch beat Alexis Terry (the fed's own North Beach table ends the belt with "VACATED"; the card has Lynch carry both). The belt came back in 2019.

epitaph: GIW's North Beach Championship: 11 reigns are served here, across 10 different champions, the first beginning on 20 March 2011 with Alioth Starre and the last on 25 August 2019 with Agustin Gates. By the dates served here the longest is Michael Lynch's, 257 days from 23 June 2013, which the fed's own table counts as 54 days; of the reigns whose dates fit the table's own lengths, the longest is Alex Castellanos's, 59 days from 9 June 2011. Of these, 3 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It carries the fed's own North Beach table from 2011; the Affliction and NOX belts before it are listed beside it. It was unified into the Undisputed Championship on 7 March 2014 and crowned a new champion in August 2019.

name: Lightweight Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-ion-television
events.note: Renamed the ION Television Championship on the night of Revolt, 22 July 2010: that card says David Sinclair will announce a new name for the championship later that night (no announcement is on the card), and the card of 29 July 2010 says Jake Kennedy "won the ION Television title" the week before.

epitaph: GIW's Lightweight Championship: 2 reigns are served here, across 2 different champions, the first beginning on 15 July 2010 with Nitro and the last on 22 July 2010 with Jake Kennedy. The longest of those is Jake Kennedy's, 31 days from 22 July 2010. The first two lines of the fed's own Television history; renamed the ION Television Championship on 22 July 2010.

name: ION Television Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-television
events.note: Billed as the GIW Television Championship from the card of Revolt, 20 January 2011; no card or history line announces a change of name.

epitaph: GIW's ION Television Championship: 5 reigns are served here, across 5 different champions, the first beginning on 22 August 2010 with Megathreat and the last on 31 October 2010 with Joshua Acquin. The longest is Joshua Acquin's, from 31 October 2010 to about 9 January 2011 (71 days in the fed's own history); of the reigns with both dates exact, the longest is Tony Miranda's, 24 days from 2 September 2010. Of these, 2 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It was billed the GIW Television Championship from 20 January 2011.

name: GIW Television Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-north-beach
events.note: On the card of Exile (13 February 2011) a match was announced for the next week to merge it with the GIW NOX Championship into the GIW North Beach Championship; the unification bout of 17 February 2011 ended in a double count-out and the belt was active again in May 2011 (the fed's own history: "Activated Again by La'Sarah Audric").

Retired by Joshua Acquin, the winner of the opening match of Final Solution, 4 December 2011, under that match's terms, and returned to Joshua Acquin on 9 February 2012 (the fed's own history: "Belt Momentarily Retired, Then Returned Acquin Still Champion").
Thrown away by Chairman Matt Kluge on the card of Category 5, 1 July 2012 (the fed's own history: "Title Disposed of by Chairman Kluge"); reinstated by Aspen Chaud on 15 March 2015.

epitaph: GIW's Television Championship: 28 reigns are served here, across 23 different champions, the first beginning on 13 February 2011 with Joshua Acquin and the last on 7 September 2015 with Alexis Terry. By the dates served here the longest is Joshua Acquin's, 77 days from 4 December 2011, which the fed's own history counts as 11 days; of the reigns whose dates fit the history's own lengths, the longest is Henry Malkin's, 70 days from 19 February 2012. Of these, 7 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It was retired twice by the fed, in December 2011 and July 2012, and reinstated on 15 March 2015.

name: GIW Legacy Championship

events.note: Retired when Aspen Chaud became owner of the fed (the fed's own history: "Belt Retired when Aspen becomes Owner"); the card of 24 November 2012 introduces her as the new owner, and no card names the belt's retirement itself.

epitaph: GIW's Legacy Championship: 8 reigns are served here, across 7 different champions, the first beginning on 22 August 2010 with Jamie Vaccaro and the last on 15 August 2012 with Aspen Chaud. The longest of those is Alexis Terry's, 105 days from 15 January 2012. Of these, 1 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It was made at Blackout on 22 August 2010 by the unification of the Hardcore and Affliction belts, and retired in November 2012.

name: GIW Hardcore Championship

events.title: giw-galveston-2010-legacy
events.note: Unified with the Affliction Championship into the GIW Legacy Championship on the card of Blackout, 22 August 2010.

epitaph: GIW's Hardcore Championship: 4 reigns are served here, across 4 different champions, the first beginning on 18 July 2010 with Billy Spizatoni and the last on 21 September 2015 with George Stark. The longest of those is Jamie Vaccaro's, 32 days from 21 July 2010. Of these, 3 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It was unified into the Legacy Championship in 2010; the fed's own history then has it retired, reinstated by David Sinclair and vacated at the 2015 hiatus.

name: GIW Tag Team Championship

events.note: Retired with Matt Kluge on the card of Blackout II, 11 September 2011 ("all the belts will be retired with him"); reinstated by Blake Beckett on 5 January 2012.
Retired with the division on the card of 9 February 2012 after Seth Ramsey was hurt (the fed's own history: "Seth Ramsey Injured, Belts Momentarily Retired"); brought back in April 2015.

epitaph: GIW's Tag Team Championship: 12 reigns are served here, across 10 different champions, the first beginning on 28 November 2010 with Technical Mechanica and the last on 19 July 2015 with The Setons. The longest of those is Perfect Combination's, 77 days from 3 May 2015. Of these, 6 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). It was retired by the fed in September 2011 and February 2012 and brought back in April 2015.

name: GIW Women's Championship

events.note: Retired on the card of Revolt, 11 November 2010, with the fed's own history reading "Title Retired" ("the GIW Women's Championship will be RETIRED once and for all").

epitaph: GIW's Women's Championship: 5 reigns are served here, across 5 different champions, the first beginning on 11 July 2010 with Violet Vanity and the last on 26 August 2010 with Kacie Church. The longest is Kacie Church's, from 26 August 2010 to about 11 November 2010 (78 days in the fed's own history); of the reigns with both dates exact, the longest is Alexii Ravynova's, 18 days from 4 August 2010. Of these, 2 ended outside a match (stripped, vacated or retired). Its cards call it the Divas title and the Galveston Island Women's title side by side in 2010; it was retired on 11 November 2010.
